lessons.title: SLIs
lessons.summary: What does an SLI measure? An aspect of service behavior experienced by users.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Choose a measurement population and a precise definition.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A dashboard tracks CPU but users report failed checkouts. Define a checkout success indicator from eligible requests.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An SLI is always a contractual penalty. This is not a sound assumption; an aspect of service behavior experienced by users.

lessons.takeaway: Choose a measurement population and a precise definition.

lessons.title: SLOs
lessons.summary: What does an SLO specify? A target for an SLI over a defined window.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Targets should reflect user needs and business trade-offs.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Teams argue over whether current reliability is sufficient. Agree on a measurable target and evaluation window.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An SLO guarantees that outages cannot happen. This is not a sound assumption; a target for an SLI over a defined window.

lessons.takeaway: Targets should reflect user needs and business trade-offs.

lessons.title: Error budgets
lessons.summary: What is an error budget? The allowed unreliability implied by an SLO.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Budget policy connects reliability performance to release decisions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A service exhausts its error budget during repeated risky releases. Apply the agreed reliability policy and prioritize stabilization.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It is a budget for buying monitoring software. This is not a sound assumption; the allowed unreliability implied by an SLO.

lessons.takeaway: Budget policy connects reliability performance to release decisions.

lessons.title: Incident roles
lessons.summary: Why assign an incident commander? To coordinate decisions roles and communication.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Coordination can be separate from hands-on diagnosis.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Several responders make conflicting production changes. Establish coordination and track owners of mitigation actions.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: The commander must personally execute every command. This is not a sound assumption; to coordinate decisions roles and communication.

lessons.takeaway: Coordination can be separate from hands-on diagnosis.

lessons.title: Mitigation
lessons.summary: What is the immediate priority during an active user-impacting outage? Reduce impact while preserving useful evidence.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Root-cause investigation can continue after stabilization.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A recent release is strongly correlated with failures and rollback is safe. Evaluate and execute the known rollback while monitoring recovery.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A full root-cause report must precede every mitigation. This is not a sound assumption; reduce impact while preserving useful evidence.

lessons.takeaway: Root-cause investigation can continue after stabilization.

lessons.title: Postmortems
lessons.summary: What is the purpose of a blameless postmortem? Learn how system conditions enabled an incident.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Useful actions have owners and verifiable outcomes.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: The same outage recurs after a report with vague recommendations. Create specific owned improvements and track completion.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Blameless means avoiding any discussion of decisions. This is not a sound assumption; learn how system conditions enabled an incident.

lessons.takeaway: Useful actions have owners and verifiable outcomes.

lessons.title: Toil
lessons.summary: Which work best matches SRE toil? Repetitive operational work that scales with service growth.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Not all valuable operational work is toil.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Engineers manually perform the same routine provisioning each day. Measure the repetition and evaluate safe automation.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every manual task is necessarily worthless. This is not a sound assumption; repetitive operational work that scales with service growth.

lessons.takeaway: Not all valuable operational work is toil.

lessons.title: Runbooks
lessons.summary: What makes a runbook useful during an incident? Clear symptoms evidence actions and escalation criteria.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Runbooks need ownership and periodic validation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A responder follows an old procedure and worsens an outage. Validate the procedure and add bounded steps with stop conditions.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A long untested command list is sufficient. This is not a sound assumption; clear symptoms evidence actions and escalation criteria.

lessons.takeaway: Runbooks need ownership and periodic validation.

lessons.title: Burn rate
lessons.summary: What does an error-budget burn rate greater than one indicate? Budget is being consumed faster than the sustainable SLO rate.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Burn rate must be interpreted with its measurement window.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A brief spike triggers pages despite negligible long-term budget impact. Evaluate multiwindow burn-rate alerts against meaningful budget consumption.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It always means the entire budget is already exhausted. This is not a sound assumption; budget is being consumed faster than the sustainable SLO rate.

lessons.takeaway: Burn rate must be interpreted with its measurement window.

lessons.title: Latency indicators
lessons.summary: Why can average latency hide poor user experience? A small slow tail can be masked by many fast requests.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Latency targets should define thresholds and relevant populations.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Mean latency is stable but a subset of users sees long delays. Inspect latency distribution and affected cohorts.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: The average always equals the slowest request. This is not a sound assumption; a small slow tail can be masked by many fast requests.

lessons.takeaway: Latency targets should define thresholds and relevant populations.

lessons.title: Alert actionability
lessons.summary: What should a paging alert usually imply? A human action is needed within a relevant response time.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Nonurgent information can often become a ticket or dashboard.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Responders receive hundreds of nonactionable overnight alerts. Review pages for impact urgency and an actionable response.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every metric anomaly must page immediately. This is not a sound assumption; a human action is needed within a relevant response time.

lessons.takeaway: Nonurgent information can often become a ticket or dashboard.

lessons.title: Capacity headroom
lessons.summary: Why maintain capacity headroom? To absorb demand variation failures and recovery work.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Capacity planning should include loss of a failure domain.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: One zone fails and surviving instances immediately saturate. Evaluate remaining capacity under the failure scenario.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Average demand alone is sufficient for all capacity decisions. This is not a sound assumption; to absorb demand variation failures and recovery work.

lessons.takeaway: Capacity planning should include loss of a failure domain.

lessons.title: Load shedding
lessons.summary: What is the goal of load shedding? Reject some work to protect useful service under overload.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Prioritization and bounded queues can preserve critical traffic.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A backend is overloaded and queues grow without bound. Bound the queue and shed lower-priority work with clear signals.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Accepting every request always improves availability. This is not a sound assumption; reject some work to protect useful service under overload.

lessons.takeaway: Prioritization and bounded queues can preserve critical traffic.

lessons.title: Backpressure
lessons.summary: What does backpressure communicate? Downstream capacity constraints to upstream producers.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Producer behavior must respond to the signal to be effective.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A queue grows faster than workers can drain it. Limit producer rate or increase sustainable processing capacity.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Backpressure creates unlimited downstream capacity. This is not a sound assumption; downstream capacity constraints to upstream producers.

lessons.takeaway: Producer behavior must respond to the signal to be effective.

lessons.title: Retry storms
lessons.summary: Why can layered retries multiply load? Each layer may repeat work already being retried elsewhere.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Retry policies need an end-to-end budget.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Three service layers each retry failed calls several times. Coordinate retry ownership and bound total attempts.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Retries at every layer always reduce traffic. This is not a sound assumption; each layer may repeat work already being retried elsewhere.

lessons.takeaway: Retry policies need an end-to-end budget.

lessons.title: Recovery testing
lessons.summary: What demonstrates that a backup is operationally useful? A successful verified restore meeting recovery requirements.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Backup completion alone does not prove recoverability.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Backups succeed but no one has restored the current application version. Run an isolated restore exercise and verify data and service behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A green backup job guarantees any restore will work. This is not a sound assumption; a successful verified restore meeting recovery requirements.

lessons.takeaway: Backup completion alone does not prove recoverability.

lessons.title: RTO
lessons.summary: What does a recovery time objective describe? The target duration to restore service after disruption.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Recovery dependencies and human steps contribute to elapsed recovery time.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A recovery plan promises one hour but identity recovery takes two hours. Exercise the complete dependency chain and revise the plan.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It specifies the maximum acceptable data-loss window. This is not a sound assumption; the target duration to restore service after disruption.

lessons.takeaway: Recovery dependencies and human steps contribute to elapsed recovery time.

lessons.title: RPO
lessons.summary: What does a recovery point objective describe? The acceptable data-loss window after a disruption.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Replication lag and backup frequency affect achievable recovery points.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A restore loses six hours of writes despite a one-hour RPO. Compare backup and replication behavior with the required loss window.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It is the maximum allowed service restart time. This is not a sound assumption; the acceptable data-loss window after a disruption.

lessons.takeaway: Replication lag and backup frequency affect achievable recovery points.

lessons.title: Canary releases
lessons.summary: Why use a canary rollout? Limit exposure while comparing a new version with a baseline.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Canary metrics must represent meaningful user impact.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A new version raises error rates only for one request category. Compare relevant cohorts and stop or roll back the canary.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A canary proves there can be no production defects. This is not a sound assumption; limit exposure while comparing a new version with a baseline.

lessons.takeaway: Canary metrics must represent meaningful user impact.

lessons.title: Feature flags
lessons.summary: What operational benefit can a feature flag provide? Disable a behavior independently of redeploying the whole binary.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Flags need ownership lifecycle management and tested fallback paths.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A newly enabled feature causes a dependency overload. Disable the flag if its fallback is safe and verify recovery.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Flags automatically undo irreversible data mutations. This is not a sound assumption; disable a behavior independently of redeploying the whole binary.

lessons.takeaway: Flags need ownership lifecycle management and tested fallback paths.

lessons.title: Dependencies
lessons.summary: Why map critical service dependencies? Shared dependencies can create correlated failures.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Dependency health should be understood from the caller's perspective.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Several services fail after a shared identity system outage. Investigate the common dependency and caller failure behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Independent service names guarantee independent failure modes. This is not a sound assumption; shared dependencies can create correlated failures.

lessons.takeaway: Dependency health should be understood from the caller's perspective.

lessons.title: Graceful degradation
lessons.summary: What is graceful degradation? Preserving important functions when some capabilities fail.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Fallback behavior should be explicitly designed and tested.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Recommendations fail but checkout can work without them. Serve checkout with the optional recommendation feature degraded.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It means reporting success for every failed request. This is not a sound assumption; preserving important functions when some capabilities fail.

lessons.takeaway: Fallback behavior should be explicitly designed and tested.

lessons.title: Chaos experiments
lessons.summary: What makes a resilience experiment controlled? A hypothesis limited scope and explicit abort conditions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Start with safe scope and measurable steady-state behavior.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A team proposes an unbounded production failure test. Define a hypothesis blast radius and stop conditions first.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Randomly breaking production is sufficient experiment design. This is not a sound assumption; a hypothesis limited scope and explicit abort conditions.

lessons.takeaway: Start with safe scope and measurable steady-state behavior.

lessons.title: Incident communication
lessons.summary: Why publish regular incident updates? Stakeholders need consistent impact and recovery information.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Uncertainty should be stated rather than replaced with invented certainty.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Support receives conflicting guesses from different responders. Assign a communication owner and publish evidence-based updates.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Only a final root cause is worth communicating. This is not a sound assumption; stakeholders need consistent impact and recovery information.

lessons.takeaway: Uncertainty should be stated rather than replaced with invented certainty.

lessons.title: SLO aggregation
lessons.summary: Why can a global success rate hide important failures? High-volume healthy traffic can mask a failing user segment.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Segmented indicators can complement an overall SLO.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: One region is down but global availability remains above target. Inspect region and critical-journey indicators alongside the global metric.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An overall SLO guarantees every region meets the same target. This is not a sound assumption; high-volume healthy traffic can mask a failing user segment.

lessons.takeaway: Segmented indicators can complement an overall SLO.

lessons.title: Overload recovery
lessons.summary: Why can recovery traffic worsen an outage? Retries cache warming and reconnects add demand during recovery.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Recovery should be staged within available capacity.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A restored service is overwhelmed by reconnecting clients. Ramp traffic and control retries while observing saturation.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Restarting every instance simultaneously always restores service fastest. This is not a sound assumption; retries cache warming and reconnects add demand during recovery.

lessons.takeaway: Recovery should be staged within available capacity.

lessons.title: Consistency trade-offs
lessons.summary: Why make consistency requirements explicit? Failure behavior depends on which guarantees the application needs.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Different operations can require different consistency guarantees.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A partition forces a decision for account-balance updates. Prioritize the required correctness guarantee and define failure behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every distributed operation can always be available and strongly consistent during partitions. This is not a sound assumption; failure behavior depends on which guarantees the application needs.

lessons.takeaway: Different operations can require different consistency guarantees.

lessons.title: Reliability investment
lessons.summary: How should reliability work be prioritized? By user impact risk and expected reduction of recurring failure.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Frequency duration and blast radius all influence value.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A rare failure affects all customers while frequent minor alerts affect none. Compare impact and risk before selecting the next engineering project.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: The newest monitoring tool is always the highest-value investment. This is not a sound assumption; by user impact risk and expected reduction of recurring failure.

lessons.takeaway: Frequency duration and blast radius all influence value.

lessons.title: Incident metrics
lessons.summary: Why is a single average recovery time insufficient? It can hide distribution incident severity and changing classification.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Metrics need stable definitions and contextual interpretation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A dashboard improves after severe incidents are reclassified away. Audit definitions and inspect distributions by comparable incident class.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A lower average always proves every incident class improved. This is not a sound assumption; it can hide distribution incident severity and changing classification.

lessons.takeaway: Metrics need stable definitions and contextual interpretation.

lessons.title: Safe automation
lessons.summary: What should high-impact remediation automation include? Bounded scope verification and a safe stop or rollback path.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Automation can amplify mistakes as quickly as successful actions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An automated restart loop repeatedly disrupts healthy instances. Add evidence-based guards cooldowns and post-action checks.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Automated actions are inherently safer than manual actions. This is not a sound assumption; bounded scope verification and a safe stop or rollback path.

lessons.takeaway: Automation can amplify mistakes as quickly as successful actions.
